A1.justification: Both 24-page PDFs describe METEORA and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A-H. Content can be matched reliably despite extensive rewriting and display changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original context-prioritization, answer-generation, poisoning-detection, component-ablation, and runtime results across six datasets.

after.justification: v4 retains original retrieval, generation, and poisoning results and reports additional baseline comparisons and ablation outcomes.

M1.justification: The DPO rationale generator, evidence pairing, pooled embeddings with elbow detection, neighboring-evidence expansion, and Verifier remain. v4 groups pooling within pairing and makes expansion explicitly optional, but non-expanded configurations were already evaluated in v1. The conservative Verifier instructions and previous-evidence summaries were already documented in v1 Appendix A.3.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ContractNLI, PrivacyQA, CUAD, MAUD, FinQA, and QASPER on context prioritization, answer generation, and corpus-poisoning defense. The added models, controls, and comparative illustration do not establish additional dataset, domain, or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 expands from five to eight external CP comparators, adding SBERT E5-Large-v2, Cross-Encoder BGE-Reranker-Large, and RankLLaMA 7b. Fine-Tuned SBERT disappears from the generation comparison corresponding to v1 Figure 6 and v4 Figure 4. The Domain-Specific LLM comparator plotted in v1 Figure 2 also disappears.

E3.justification: The new without-DPO control extends the evaluation design to an untuned rationale generator. Retained experiments preserve the stated top-k range, dataset-average k matching, chunk-size coverage, 30% poisoning rate, and full-model DPO split and training budget. Missing generation sample counts and per-instance poison counts in v4 do not establish that those settings changed.

E4.justification: v4 adds an ablation of DPO training and revises the expansion ablation. It removes the comparison isolating pooling's contribution and the measured runtime analysis in v1 Appendix A.6. The smaller-chunk appendix rows now called Pairing retain v1's Pairing + Pooling results, while the original pairing-only controls disappear. Figure 1 adds a comparative poisoning illustration using a retained legal example.

E5.justification: v1 Figure 6 reports variance bars and multiple trials; v4 Figure 4 additionally specifies p < 0.01 and a paired t-test. Neither version specifies run or seed counts, so this establishes additional statistical reporting, not increased replication.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds baseline and control outcomes, including average recall 0.88 without DPO and average precision 0.23 without expansion. Some retained scores change: Cross-Encoder MiniLM's FinQA precision changes from 0.12 to 0.10. Full METEORA's average CP precision/recall remains 0.19/0.93, and the principal poisoning F1 results remain unchanged. Runtime results, pairing-only outcomes, and some 512-token poisoning precision/recall entries are removed.

T1.justification: v4 adds a pipeline-level computational-complexity analysis with assumptions about evidence counts and LLM prefill cost. It corrects the pairing definition from maximum similarity values to argmax evidence and removes v1's bi-encoder/cross-encoder special-case reduction claim. The DPO definitions, derivation, convergence argument, proof, and Algorithm 1 in the appendices remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: v4 makes computational efficiency a central contribution, strengthens the evidence-reduction claim from approximately 50% to 80%, and claims freedom from LLM rerankers' context-length limitations. Its abstract introduces a 21.05% precision advantage for the no-expansion variant and reports a 13.41% recall advantage against the expanded baselines, versus v1's 14.8% recall claim. The principal generation and poisoning-defense claims are retained.

C2.justification: v4 adds substantive limitations concerning naturally incorrect versus adversarial training negatives, shared-rationale failures affecting selection and verification, and attacks on the rationale generator being outside scope. It explicitly discusses FinQA underperformance and interprets expansion through document structure and chunk boundaries. It also interprets instruction flags as procedural subversion. v1's concluding qualifications about few-shot dependence, gold contexts, and efficiency tradeoffs are removed.

D1.justification: v4 provides additional baseline identifiers and specifies QASPER's QA count as 5,049 rather than 5,000+. It removes the NVIDIA L40s hardware and batch-size-five disclosure, the 100-instances-per-dataset generation sampling and manual evaluator-check description, and the explicit one-poisoned-evidence-per-instance setting. DPO hyperparameters, prompt templates, and the anonymous code-access link remain.

R1.justification: The research positioning expands substantially around the relationship between interpretability, security, and efficiency. RADIO and Set-R receive new discussion, alongside added literature on rationale annotation, prompt injection, chunking, and inference costs. Appendix A.1 refines distinctions from MIRAGE and rationale-guided retrieval and replaces several cited works, including the GRPO reference.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten. Method explanations are reorganized and expanded, experimental subsections are consolidated, and the results narrative merges CP and generation discussion while restructuring the ablations. These are substantial language and organizational revisions even though much of the appendix text remains stable.

P2.justification: v4 adds a comparative illustration, redraws and relocates the pipeline overview, removes the encoder-comparison diagram and full precision-recall plots, expands and color-codes Table 2, merges poisoning displays, and redraws the generation chart. Appendix tables and document typography are also substantially reorganized. Figure 4's caption visibly overlaps surrounding body text in v4.

improvement.justification: Additional baselines, the DPO control, and explicit threat-model limitations improve the paper's assessability. However, v4 strengthens efficiency claims while removing v1 Table 7's measured timings, and its new complexity account omits Verifier cost. It also removes evaluation details and claims a 23.7% MAUD DPO recall gain although Table 2's 0.65 to 0.72 implies about 10.8%. Stronger comparative evidence therefore coexists with weaker support for a central efficiency claim and new interpretation errors, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
